title: Edit Distance: Repainting a Shop Sign
summary: Each cell is the fewest edits between two prefixes: free on a match, else one more than the cheapest neighbor.

analogy.scenario: A sign painter must change a shop sign from CART to ACT, one letter at a time: paint in a letter, scrape one off, or paint over one. What's the fewest changes?

mapping.real: The old sign and the new sign

takeaway.pattern: Dynamic programming (2D table over two strings)
takeaway.summary: edit[i][j] = edit[i − 1][j − 1] on a match, else 1 + min(delete, insert, replace). The edges count pure inserts and deletes.
takeaway.spaceComplexity: O(m × n), or O(n) keeping two rows
whenToUse: How different two strings are (spell check, diffs)
Three ways to change one character

scenes.narration: A sign painter must turn a sign reading CART into ACT, one change at a time: scrape a letter off, paint one in, or paint over one. What's the fewest changes?
scenes.caption: Repaint CART into ACT with the fewest changes

scenes.narration: Trying every sequence of changes explodes. Instead, work out the fewest changes for every pair of beginnings of the two signs.
scenes.caption: Trying every sequence of changes explodes

scenes.narration: Turning nothing into the first j letters takes j paintings: the top row. Turning i letters into nothing takes i scrapings: the left column.
scenes.caption: From nothing: paint letters in; to nothing: scrape them off

scenes.narration: C against A: scrape costs 1 plus 1, paint-in 1 plus 1, paint over 1 plus 0. Painting over wins: 1.
scenes.caption: C into A: painting over beats the others

scenes.narration: C against C: the letter is already right, so the cell copies its diagonal for free.
scenes.caption: C meets C: no change, copy the diagonal

scenes.narration: Turning C into A, C, T: the cheapest path paints a T onto the 1 from the left: 2.
scenes.caption: C into ACT: paint in the T

scenes.narration: A against C: all three options cost 1 plus 1. Ties go to the first tried, scraping off a letter: 2.
scenes.caption: A against C: a three-way tie, scraping goes first

scenes.narration: The last T matches, so the corner copies its diagonal: 2. Scrape off the C, then paint over the R with a C.
scenes.caption: T meets T: the whole sign takes 2 changes

scenes.narration: Scraping is delete, painting in is insert, and painting over is replace. Each cell takes the cheapest neighbor: O(m times n).
scenes.caption: Scrape, paint in, paint over: delete, insert, replace
